title: Pyraloidea (Lepidoptera) of a Mediterranean Elevational Gradient in Mersin Province, Türkiye: An Annotated Checklist with 80 New Provincial Records
content: The Pyraloidea are among the largest superfamilies of Lepidoptera, yet their distribution in the eastern Mediterranean is documented unevenly. Light-trapping was carried out on 54 nights between 2008 and 2024 at 45 localities in the districts of Erdemli and Mezitli, Mersin Province, southern Türkiye, along an elevational gradient from 150 to 1800 m a.s.l. The survey yielded 492 occurrence records of 1330 specimens belonging to 161 species in 91 genera; the Pyralidae are represented by 78 species and the Crambidae by 83, and the largest subfamilies are the Phycitinae (61 species), the Crambinae (23) and the Spilomelinae (22). Eighty species are reported for the first time from Mersin Province, the assessment being made against the national catalogue, two annotated lists for the district of Anamur, an unpublished doctoral thesis on the region and the applied entomological literature. Nomenclature was checked species by species against the Global Information System on Pyraloidea, which altered 28 entries relative to the source material and included five changes of generic placement and one synonymy. Ten of the species were described from Anatolian type localities. Species composition became increasingly dissimilar with increasing elevational distance between sampling events (Spearman ρ = 0.187, p &lt; 0.001), an effect independent of season, and 94% of the dissimilarity between assemblages was attributable to species replacement rather than to nestedness; no significant relationship between elevation and species richness per night was found once overdispersion was accounted for. Sample-based rarefaction and the Chao2 estimator indicate that about three-quarters of the pyraloid fauna likely to be present has been recorded. Neither district contains a protected area. The occurrence data are published in Darwin Core format.
